concept.body: Know the principle's edges: (1) it certifies VOLUME only — shearing keeps volume but lengthens the lateral surface along the slant; (2) its converse fails — equal volumes never imply matching cross-sections (a 1×1×12 post and a 2×2×3 block both hold 12); (3) 'equal sections at EVERY level' is strict — solids matching only at sampled heights (a barrel vs a cylinder) can differ in volume.

explanationVariants: Volume follows slices (unchanged); surface follows the boundary (stretched).

widget.prompt: A stack of books is pushed into a lean. What changes?

options.label: Volume stays the same; the outside surface of the stack grows
options.feedback: Every level keeps its book (volume); the sides now run along a slant (surface).

options.label: Both stay the same
options.feedback: The sides lengthen with the lean — surface grows even as volume holds.

options.label: Volume shrinks
options.feedback: Each book is intact at its level — volume is untouched; only surface grows.

options.label: Both grow
options.feedback: Volume reads slices, and every slice is the same book: unchanged. Surface alone grows.

steps.body: A principle is defined by its edges. Cavalieri certifies VOLUME only — shear a stack and the volume holds, but the leaning stack's outside gets LONGER: lateral surface grows with slant. And the converse fails: two solids can share a volume while their slices disagree at every single level.

explanationVariants: The lateral face of the sheared stack runs along the slant, length 13 instead of 12.
Volume equal; lateral surface larger — Cavalieri never covered it.

widget.prompt: A right prism (height 12) is sheared so its slant edge is 13 (top shifted 5). Compared to the original:

options.label: Same volume, but MORE lateral surface — the sides now run along the longer slant
options.feedback: Volume reads slices (unchanged); surface reads the boundary, which stretched from 12 to 13 along the lean. Cavalieri's silence on surfaces is deliberate.

options.label: Same volume and same surface area
options.feedback: The lateral faces lengthened with the slant (12 → 13) — surface grew even as volume held.

options.label: Less volume, same surface
options.feedback: Backwards on both: slices preserve the volume; the boundary stretched.

options.label: More volume too
options.feedback: The slices never changed — volume is exactly equal; only the surface grew.

explanationVariants: Equal volumes with UNMATCHED slices: find one example and the converse dies.
A 1×1×12 post and a 2×2×3 block both hold 12 — sections 1 vs 4.

widget.prompt: Does equal volume imply equal cross-sections at each level?

options.label: It doesn't — a 1×1×12 post and a 2×2×3 block both hold volume 12 with sections 1 and 4 (they don't even share a height)
options.feedback: One counterexample settles a converse — volume is an integral, and integrals forget the layer-by-layer details.

options.label: Yes — that's Cavalieri's principle
options.feedback: Cavalieri runs slices-to-volume; the reverse direction fails on the 12-vs-12 post-and-block pair.

options.label: Yes, for solids of the same height
options.feedback: Even same-height pairs fail: a cone and a cylinder of a third the base area share height and volume with slice-by-slice disagreement.

options.label: Only for spheres
options.feedback: There is no rescuing family for a false converse — volume equality never promises slice equality.

explanationVariants: Cavalieri's hypothesis is EVERY level — a bulge between checkpoints breaks it.
The middle bulge means sections differ somewhere: the principle never fires.

widget.prompt: A student claims a barrel equals a cylinder by Cavalieri because 'they match at the top, bottom, and they're the same height.' The error:

options.label: The barrel BULGES between the ends — sections differ at middle heights, so the every-level hypothesis fails
options.feedback: The barrel is precisely the between-checkpoints counterexample: matching ends, fatter middle, strictly more volume.

options.label: Cavalieri needs equal surface areas first
options.feedback: Surfaces never enter the hypothesis — the failure is the unmatched MIDDLE sections.

options.label: Barrels aren't solids
options.feedback: Barrels slice fine — the trouble is that their slices don't match the cylinder's at every height.

options.label: There is no error
options.feedback: There is: the bulge violates 'every level', and the barrel holds MORE than the end-matched cylinder.

widget.prompt: The sheared prism from k1 has a square 4×4 base and vertical height 12. Its volume = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 208 = 16 × 13 charges the SLANT — Cavalieri bills vertical height: 16 × 12 = 192.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Bh = 16 × 12 = 192 — while the lateral surface (running along 13) grew, this number didn't.

widget.prompt: Which conclusion is actually LICENSED by Cavalieri's principle?

options.label: A leaning cylinder holds exactly what its upright twin holds
options.feedback: Same circles at every level — the principle's home turf.

options.label: A leaning cylinder has the same lateral surface as its upright twin
options.feedback: Surface stretches with slant — outside the principle's jurisdiction.

options.label: Two tanks holding equal water have equal cross-sections
options.feedback: That's the failed converse — the post-and-block pair refutes it.

options.label: Solids matching at three heights match in volume
options.feedback: Three checkpoints aren't 'every level' — the barrel lives in the gaps.

hints: Volume: Cavalieri with vertical height. Surface: the slant does the work.
The lateral surface of the sheared square prism is 4 rectangles along the slant edge 13.
Perimeter of the base times slant: 16 × 13.
explanationVariants: Lateral surface = (perimeter)(slant) = 16 × 13 = 208 — versus the upright twin's 16 × 12 = 192. The shear added 16 of surface while adding zero volume.

widget.prompt: Same sheared prism (4×4 base, vertical height 12, slant edge 13). Its LATERAL surface area (the four side faces) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 192 is the UPRIGHT twin's lateral surface (16 × 12) — the sheared sides run along 13: 16 × 13 = 208.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Perimeter × slant = 16 × 13 = 208 — the surface pays for the lean that volume got free.

takeaways: Cavalieri certifies volume ONLY — shearing preserves volume but grows lateral surface (12 → 13 per side).
The converse fails: equal volumes never promise matching slices (post vs block).
'Every level' is strict — barrels beat end-matched cylinders in the unchecked middle.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: Cavalieri becomes the engine that JUSTIFIES the volume formulas.
